origin_and_geography.native_tract: Kankrej taluk of Banaskantha, Mehsana, Ahmedabad, Sabarkantha, and Kutch districts in North Gujarat, extending into Barmer and Jodhpur districts of Rajasthan.
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Arid to semi-arid desert border and Rann of Kutch plains.
origin_and_geography.historical_background: Known in ancient literature as the bull depicted on Indus Valley Mohenjo-Daro seals. One of the heaviest and most powerful indigenous cattle breeds of India.

morphological_traits.horns: Majestic, thick, lyre-shaped horns curving outward, upward, and slightly inward, covered with a distinct skin sheath at base.
morphological_traits.forehead: Broad, dished (concave) between the eyes with a strong poll crest.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Silver-grey to iron-grey; adult bulls have dark grey or black shading on shoulders, hump, and hindquarters.
morphological_traits.ears: Very large, open, pendulous, drooping like broad petals.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Enormous upright muscular hump; voluminous pendulous dewlap running from chin to brisket.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Massive skeletal structure, wide chest, strong heavy bones, dignified rhythmic walk known as 'Sawai Chal'.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: Dual-purpose (powerful agricultural draught and dependable dairy performance).
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: Heavy load carrying and deep plowing in sandy soils; famous for 'Sawai Chal' (stride of one-and-a-quarter).

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: Exceptional dry matter digestion on bajra (pearl millet) straw, guar, and saline pasture grasses.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Remarkable resistance to tick-borne diseases, contagious bovine pleuropneumonia, and thermal stress.
management_and_resilience.temperament: Stately, confident, powerful yet docile when handled consistently.

conservation_status: Secure and actively bred across Gujarat and Rajasthan; key contributor to global Guzerá and Brahman cattle.
